offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The ConsumerLagHigh alert's symptom is not real now and shows no sign of having happened. Since the whole stack was created at 21:47:08, the lag metric for the ledger group has read 0, and its peak over the last 10 minutes at 15-second resolution is also 0. The ledger consumer has been posting events steadily, and the money check settled in under a second with all five invariants passing. No container restarted and no consumer setting is unusual. The most likely cause is a fault in the alert itself rather than in the payments system. For example, the rule might be stale, evaluate a different metric or series, use an old offset left over from before the 21:47 redeploy, or point at a different environment. What the evidence leaves open: no lag series exists before about 21:47, so I cannot rule out a backlog of about 250 before the fresh deploy that was cleared when the stack was recreated. I also did not inspect the alert rule's expression.

evidence.shows: Lag for the ledger and payment-confirmer groups is 0 at every point from 21:47:38 to 21:52:38, and the series starts only at about 21:47.
Peak lag over the last 10 minutes, sampled every 15s, is 0 for both groups. No backlog of 250 appeared in the window.
The ledger consumer is processing events steadily (posted at about 3.4/s, plus a few already_processed), and the confirmer is processing too. Neither consumer is stalled.
The money check settled in 0.79s, all 1113 events were posted exactly once, the ledger is balanced and matches the provider, and payments and refunds agree with the provider.
Every container was created at 21:47:08 with normal settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter). There is no recent deploy to blame.
All services are running and healthy with 0 restarts. There is no consumer crash loop that could have built a backlog.

proposed_fix.summary: No change to the payments system. Review the ConsumerLagHigh rule: check its expression, data source and environment, and check whether it read stale offsets from before the 21:47 redeploy. Then silence or resolve the alert, and keep watching ledger lag.
